summary.text: Gregory Murphy is the Republican U.S. representative for North Carolina's 3rd Congressional District, and is seeking re-election. A urologic surgeon and former state legislator, he served in the North Carolina House from 2015 to 2019 and has represented the district in Congress since a 2019 special election. He serves on the House Ways and Means, Veterans' Affairs, and House Administration committees.

paragraphs.text: Gregory Murphy was born in Raleigh, North Carolina, where he grew up, and graduated magna cum laude from Davidson College in 1985.

He earned his medical degree from the University of North Carolina School of Medicine, graduating with honors and as a member of Alpha Omega Alpha, then completed a surgical residency in urology and renal transplantation at the University of Kentucky.

Murphy practiced as a urologist in Greenville, North Carolina. His official biography says he was president of Eastern Urological Associates, an affiliate professor of surgery and chief of the Division of Urology at the East Carolina University School of Medicine, and chief of staff of Vidant Medical Center for three years.

According to that biography, he has served as a medical missionary on trips to countries including India, Nicaragua, Haiti, and several in Africa, and was Davidson College's alumni president and a member of its board of trustees.

Murphy served in the North Carolina House of Representatives, District 9, from 2015 to 2019. His official biography says he was Senior Chair of Health Policy and Chair of Health and Human Services Appropriations and was primary author of the STOP Act and HOPE Act, state opioid-response measures.
He won the July 9, 2019 Republican primary runoff over Joan Perry in the special election to succeed the late Rep. Walter B. Jones Jr., and was sworn into the U.S. House on September 15, 2019.

In Congress he serves on the House Ways and Means Committee (Health and Trade subcommittees), the Veterans' Affairs Committee (Health Subcommittee), and the Committee on House Administration (Oversight Subcommittee).
He co-chairs the House Republican Doctors Caucus and the Academic Medicine Caucus, and describes himself as the only actively practicing physician in Congress.
